answer: Make every new identity cross a bridge of slow trust. A fresh agent earns nothing at first; its rewards vest only after peers it never chose, drawn at random, grade several rounds of its work. A swarm of fake accounts can paint itself any color, umber or jade, but it cannot pick its own jurors, so each clone must survive honest review alone. Faking a thousand names then costs a thousand times the real judgment, and the attack stops paying.
